We need to determine number of methyl (CH3) groups in the sample's molecule. We have no direct description of molecule. We can get NMR spectra to infer. Use proton NMR to see signals for methyl groups (singlet, doublet, etc). Could also use carbon NMR to see number of distinct methyl carbons. Probably easiest: get proton NMR and count peaks around 0.9-1.2 ppm typical for CH3. But need to differentiate overlapping. Could also get carbon NMR for signals around 10-30 ppm typical for methyl carbons.

We need to minimize experiments. Maybe just get carbon NMR and count distinct methyl carbon signals. But if there are equivalent methyl groups they appear as one signal. The question likely asks total number of methyl groups, not distinct types. So need to count total CH3 groups, not just signals. Could use integration of proton NMR. So we need proton NMR with integration.

Thus we should call proton_nmr_spectra tool.
